name: American International Group
description: AIG is now essentially a commercial and personal property-casualty insurer: since it sold down Corebridge (its former life and retirement arm, deconsolidated 2024-06-09) it reports three General Insurance segments and a small Other Operations bucket. Clients range from multinationals to individuals in over 200 countries and jurisdictions, served through brokers, agents and other distributors. It earns premium less claims and expenses (2025 General Insurance combined ratio 90.1 percent) plus investment income on the float (net investment income $3,433M). It still holds about 10.1 percent of Corebridge stock (at 2025-12-31), whose dividends and market value changes flow through net income, and in February 2026 bought a 35 percent stake in specialty insurer Convex for $2.1 billion and 9.9 percent of asset manager Onex for $642 million.

employees.note: Approximately 22,100 employees in about 45 countries: 27 percent North America, 47 percent Asia Pacific, 26 percent EMEA.

businessLines.name: North America Commercial
businessLines.how: Sells commercial property, casualty, workers compensation, financial lines (D&O, cyber) and programs business to U.S. and Canadian companies, mostly through brokers, for annual premiums; profit is premium less claims and expenses plus investment income on the float.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), underwriting income (before net investment income)

businessLines.name: International Commercial
businessLines.how: Sells commercial property, casualty, financial lines and global specialty (marine, energy, aviation, political risk, trade credit) outside North America, including through Talbot at Lloyd's; annual premiums, largely in local currencies.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), underwriting income (before net investment income)

businessLines.name: Global Personal
businessLines.how: Sells personal auto and homeowners in selected markets, travel and accident and health, extended warranty and device protection, and high-net-worth cover (Private Client Select); premiums fell 12 percent in 2025 and the combined ratio of 99.0 percent leaves almost no underwriting profit.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), underwriting income (before net investment income)

businessLines.name: Other Operations (incl. Corebridge stake)
businessLines.how: Not an underwriting line: net investment income on the parent liquidity portfolio ($349M), dividends on the retained Corebridge stake, less corporate expenses and interest expense.

brands.name: Private Client Select
brands.note: U.S. high-net-worth personal lines; not broken out

brands.name: Corebridge Financial (AIG holds 10.1 percent at 2025-12-31; deconsolidated 2024-06-09 when AIG held 48.4 percent)
brands.note: Life and retirement business, fair-value-accounted investment; revenue no longer in AIG totals.

brands.name: Convex Group (35 percent equity interest bought 2026-02-06 for $2.1 billion)
brands.note: Global specialty insurer; AIG also reinsures 7.5 percent, 10 percent and 12.5 percent of its portfolio in 2026, 2027 and 2028.

brands.name: Onex Corporation (9.9 percent stake for $642M, restricted from sale until 2029-02-06)
Talbot Underwriting (Lloyd's managing agent), Glatfelter Insurance Group, Western World Insurance, Lexington, National Union
brands.note: operating companies named in the 10-K; premiums not broken out

whatsNext.text: Reinsurance quota share with Convex steps up from 7.5 percent (2026) to 10 percent (2027) and 12.5 percent (2028) of its portfolio
